concepts.def: One event does not affect the other's probability
P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events

walkthroughs.body_html:
Events are independent when one does NOT change the chance of the other.

Examples: tossing a coin twice, rolling two dice, picking a card and putting it back.

P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)

So P(two heads on two coins) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

A tree diagram shows every outcome of two (or more) trials. Each branch carries a probability.

Multiply along branches to find the probability of a path.

Add path totals if a question asks for more than one path (e.g. "exactly one head").

Tip: probabilities on branches from the same point should add to 1.

If you pick an item, look at it, and put it back, the bag is unchanged for the next pick. So probabilities stay the same.

Example: a bag has 4 red and 6 blue counters. Pick one, replace it, pick again.

P(red then red) = 4/10 × 4/10 = 16/100 = 4/25.
